messages:
morgan: Heads-up — we just got three returned nodes from the colo flagged as "flaky" during provider validation. IDs: rwd-gpu-12a, rwd-gpu-12b, rwd-gpu-12c. Provider saw intermittent Xid 31 and ECC counter bumps. I want a reproducible burn-in/soak plan before we put any of them back in service. Ticket #INC-4821.
arjun: Can you paste the short logs? quick triage approach: cheap fast tests first (memtest, short CUDA stress), then longer soak if intermittent fails.
sasha: Log excerpt from rwd-gpu-12b (yesterday):
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:08Z] nvidia: Xid (31): PID 1234 name: python
[2026-03-16T03:12:08Z] kernel: GPU 0 ECC single-bit 1->3
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.mode.current,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv
GPU0, Enabled, 3
```
It's small info but repeated twice over 8 hours.
lee: For reproducibility we should run a 48h mixed workload soak that includes: 1) memtestG80 6h, 2) cuda-heavy synthetic (matrix multiply + random tensors) 12h, 3) power/thermal cycling (idle->full-load loops) 8 cycles, 4) longer 24h open-run for intermittent. Fail if any Xid or ECC delta >0 during the soak period.
tay: 48h per node is a lot; we have capacity constraints in us-west. Cost/backfill: a dedicated test slot costs ~ $52/day in our internal accounting. If we quarantine 3 nodes for 48h that's ~ $312. We should triage quick then escalate.
arjun: Agree. Proposed workflow:
- Phase A (fast triage, 2-4h): run memtestG80 (4 passes), short CUDA stress (stress-cuda --duration 2h), run microbench with KV-cache stress. If clear -> Phase B.
- Phase B (extended soak, 24-72h): mixed synthetic + real workload replay from last week (sample 5% of production traces) with temp cycling every 3h.
- Logging: capture `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q` every 5m, and full core dumps on Xid.
- Acceptance: 72h with zero new Xid and ECC counters unchanged = return to pool; otherwise drain and RMA.
sasha: Added the minimal repro commands to the ticket:
```
# phase A
memtestG80 --gpu=0 --passes=4
stress-cuda --duration=7200 --matrix=8192
# monitoring
watch -n 300 'nvidia-smi -q | egrep "Ecc|Xid|Temperature"'
```
deploy-bot: Job queued: soak-runner @ rwd-gpu-12b, Phase A scheduled at 2026-03-17T09:00Z (job id soak-20260317-09-12b).
morgan: Thanks — put rwd-gpu-12b into quarantine and start phase A. If it passes, we can decide on 24h vs 72h based on repeatability. Please annotate ticket with pass/fail and attach `nvidia-smi` dumps.
lee: One more: add thermal telemetry from BMC (if available) to correlate with ECC spikes. Also run a short ECC self-test: `nvidia-persistenced` + gpu stress while toggling ECC (if vendor supports) to see if error counters are noisy.
tay: If nodes fail Phase A we should avoid long soaks and just RMA; intermittent but immediate Xid spikes on short runs usually mean hardware fault. Save us time/cost.
arjun: Also check host-level errors: PCIe resets, IOMMU messages in kernel logs, and any firmware mismatch. Add commands:
```
journalctl -k -o short-iso | egrep "NVRM|Xid|IOMMU|PCIe"
lspci -vvv | egrep "Kernel driver in use|LnkSta"
```
sasha: Ran Phase A on 12b — 2h stress completed, 0 Xid in that window, ECC stayed at 3 (no delta). Pushed nvidia-smi dumps into ticket. Scheduling Phase B 24h run starting now. :thumbsup:
morgan: Good. If 12b passes 24h, consider putting back with canary label for 72h (route <=5% traffic). If fail, mark for replacement. Can someone update the RMA playbook with the pass/fail criteria? (quick note in doc: pass=72h no Xid, ECC delta=0)
lee: I'll update playbook and add a small checklist for on-call to run quick triage before accepting provider returns.
tay: FYI — re: cost, if we start 24h soaks in us-west queue, please stagger by 6h to smooth capacity.
arjun: Noted. I'll add automation to the soak-runner to stagger starts and auto-attach logs to ticket.
morgan: Perfect. Thanks all. Keep updates minimal here — ping me on the ticket for final decision.
